chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “For the heart, when it is struck with trembling and the person’s mind departs, there is the diyyah.”
And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “For al-sa'ar there is the diyyah, and al-sa'ar is that his neck is bent so that it turns to one side.”

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial compensation due for bodily injury or killing
key_terms.الصَّعَرِ: a deforming condition in which the neck becomes bent
key_terms.الْقَلْبِ: the heart, mentioned here as the site of a grave injury
key_terms.رُعِدَ: was afflicted with trembling or violent disturbance
key_terms.فَطَارَ: departed or was lost, here indicating loss of mental stability or composure

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on diyyah for severe injury to the heart or for a neck deformity in Shi'a hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning compensation for severe bodily injuries. It states that full diyyah is due in cases of grave internal harm affecting a person’s mental state and in the deforming injury called al-sa'ar, where the neck becomes bent to one side.
